title: Port shutdown during a sanctions fight
one_line: A port intrusion enables container theft during a sanctions dispute, while the governments weigh attribution and conditional cooperation.

a.name: Bay Republic
a.private_brief: Your largest port has stopped moving cargo two weeks after your government tightened sanctions on Hill Federation. Three containers tied to a smuggling case disappeared during manual operations. Exporters are losing money by the hour and the president wants a response before markets open.
a.objective: Restore port operations, recover the missing containers, and punish the responsible actor without turning political motive into proof.

b.name: Hill Federation
b.private_brief: A Hill cabinet economic-security office secretly commissioned a smuggling network to disrupt Bay's port and extract selected containers. No military unit ran the intrusion, but your government authorized it. Your cabinet wants sanctions relief and fears exposure of its contractor arrangement.
b.objective: Protect Hill interests, avoid retaliation, and seek sanctions talks while preserving a route to recover cargo and share evidence. Do not treat political benefit as proof or promise to speak for Bay.

mediator_brief: You represent a maritime security forum that both governments use for incident notifications. You can authenticate agency documents, pass private messages, and ask one member service to check a named item. You cannot lift sanctions or direct law enforcement.

postures.label: Collect evidence and keep public options open
Harden systems and use the hotline
Deliver a private warning or demand

episodes.public_event: The scheduling and gate systems at Bay's largest container port fail. Hill state media praises the disruption as deserved punishment for new sanctions. No official claims responsibility.

a.content: The intruder entered through an unpatched file-transfer server and disabled scheduling services.
Three containers tied to a smuggling network left through a manual gate during the outage.

b.content: A cabinet economic-security office authorized the smuggling network's port operation. No military unit conducted the intrusion, but the cabinet office commissioned it.
The port outage gives Hill leverage to demand sanctions talks, but exporters fear Bay retaliation.

mediator.content: Vessels are diverting, but emergency cargo can still enter through a secondary terminal.

episodes.public_event: A customs custody receipt appears online claiming that manual-gate images are preserved for an inquiry. The three containers remain missing. Bay considers relying on the images for attribution. Hill offers technical help if Bay opens sanctions talks.

a.content: Customs has preserved a complete, unaltered copy of the manual-gate images in its evidence vault and can provide a supervised mirror to the joint inquiry.
One command server was used by a Hill maritime-ministry contractor six months ago.

b.content: The contractor stopped using the command server five months ago. The server was later resold.

mediator.content: The customs evidence custodian can check the receipt signature and whether the gate-image copy was deposited if asked.

episodes.public_event: The port begins partial recovery. Police find one missing truck, but the containers remain missing. Bay receives an independent attribution report before its press window; Hill threatens reciprocal sanctions if named.

a.content: The containers left in trucks controlled by the smuggling network. A lost employee card opened the gate.
The outage began four minutes before a smuggling coordinator called the drivers. Custody-checked instructions and payments link this operation to Hill's cabinet economic-security office.

b.content: The smuggling network paid a criminal access broker one week before the port outage.

mediator.content: The truck ownership and access-broker lead are independently corroborated.

P01.content: The intrusion path through the file-transfer server is confirmed.

P03.content: The containers left during the outage and remain missing.

P06.content: The customs evidence custodian authenticates the receipt and confirms that the complete gate-image copy is preserved and available for supervised inspection. This does not say the containers were recovered or identify the intrusion's sponsor.

P05.content: The old contractor link is real, but control of the server changed months before the attack.

P08.content: The truck ownership and gate route are confirmed.

P09.content: The intrusion timeline, cabinet instructions and payments for the port operation are authenticated.

H01.content: Authenticated cabinet instructions show that Hill commissioned the smuggling operation through an economic-security office.

H03.content: The contractor's access ended before the server was resold.

ground_truth.note: Hill officials commissioned the smuggling network to disable port screening and remove the containers; the network hired criminal access operators. Document authenticity is independently assigned: genuine. The document concerns a specific containment or custody claim, not attribution. If fabricated, the forger's identity is unspecified.
